extracted.intended_audience: state environmental regulators, reliability coordinators (RCs)/balancing authorities, electric utility owners/operators of affected EGUs, EPA regional staff, and FERC
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and approvable language for states to include reliability-related mechanisms in state plans implementing EPA emission standards for existing and new affected electric generating units (EGUs), including short-term emergency flexibility and temporary retirements/extensions. Covers eligibility, thresholds, documentation, and interagency review requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RULOF to address reliability/resource adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: States may use the RULOF provisions to address circumstances in which reliability or resource adequacy is a concern where considerations for a particular EGU differ from those considered when developing these emission guidelines, which may make it unreasonable for an affected EGU to comply by the prescribed date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments under RULOF are expected to take the form of different compliance timelines; RULOF is relevant at the stage of establishing standards of performance and compliance schedules and can be used via the state planning or revision processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission averaging, trading, and unit-specific mass-based compliance (voluntary)
rubrics_metrics.description: States have the ability to use emission averaging or trading, as well as unit-specific mass-based compliance, which may provide reliability-related benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These flexibilities are voluntary and may be employed provided the state demonstrates their programs achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction compared with unit-specific application of rate-based standards and apply requirements relevant to the particular flexibility (see section X.D). States decide whether to allow these in state plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1-year compliance date extension for control technology installation delays
rubrics_metrics.description: States may incorporate a mechanism to allow compliance date extensions up to 1 year for an existing affected EGU that is in the process of installing a control technology to meet its standard of performance if the source demonstrates a delay in construction or implementation resulting from causes entirely outside the owner or operator's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of qualifying delays include delays in obtaining a final construction permit after a timely/complete application or documented supply chain issues (e.g., backlog for step-up transformer equipment). The source must show it took necessary steps with sufficient lead time and that the problems were entirely outside its control and not caused by the source's actions/inactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and documentation for compliance date extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an owner/operator encounters a delay outside their control preventing compliance, the affected EGU must follow the procedures outlined in the state plan for documenting the basis for the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state plan should specify the process and required documentary evidence demonstrating the delay and efforts to comply; this is a condition to obtain the up-to-1-year extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions greater than 1 year require state plan revision using RULOF
rubrics_metrics.description: Any delay necessitating a compliance date extension of more than 1 year must be addressed via a state plan revision to adjust the compliance schedule using RULOF as a basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RULOF process and justification must be used for adjustments beyond the 1-year extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term reliability mechanism — event threshold (EEA-2 and EEA-3 only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The short-term reliability mechanism is only applicable during an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) level 2 or 3 as defined by NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-2 (or successor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEA-2 and EEA-3 better represent rare or truly emergency conditions; EEA-1 is excluded because it is preparatory, more discretionary, more frequent/opaque in reporting, and could create perverse incentives if used as a threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term mechanism — eligible units (called upon/instructed units only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only specific units that are called upon or otherwise instructed to increase output beyond planned day-ahead or near-term expected output, or asked to remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch during an EEA-2 or EEA-3 event, are eligible for the short-term reliability flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires proper documentation (see reporting requirements). Geographic/regional applicability matters because EEAs often affect limited zones; for large-scale events a broader group of sources may be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term mechanism — treatment for new sources
rubrics_metrics.description: For new sources, emissions and/or generation data produced during discrete EEA-2 or EEA-3 events will not be counted when determining applicability and the source's Phase 1 standard of performance may be used for compliance determinations through the duration of these events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New-source compliance remains on an annual (or rolling annual) basis overall; the mechanism allows temporary exclusion of event data for applicability/compliance while the event is documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term mechanism — treatment for existing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: For existing sources, states may temporarily apply an alternative standard of performance or allow the unit to apply its baseline emission rate in lieu of its standard of performance for the hours of operation corresponding to the duration of the alert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When demonstrating annual compliance, the existing affected EGU would demonstrate compliance based on application of its baseline emission performance rate for the documented hours it operated under a revised schedule due to an EEA-2 or EEA-3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term mechanism — annual compliance still required
rubrics_metrics.description: These final emission guidelines require compliance with standards of performance on an annual basis (or rolling annual average for new sources), not on shorter periods such as hourly, daily, or monthly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This annual compliance period provides significant flexibility for sources whose emission performance may change temporarily (including in response to grid emergency conditions), and the short-term mechanism is an additional safeguard for rare emergency events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term mechanism — required supplemental reporting, recordkeeping, and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: States and affected sources must supply documentation when using the short-term mechanism: (1) documentation that the EEA was in effect from the entity issuing the alert, with exact duration; (2) documentation that the EEA included the affected source/region; and (3) documentation that the source was instructed to increase output beyond planned day-ahead or near-term expected output and/or asked to remain in operation outside scheduled dispatch from a reliability coordinator, balancing authority, or ISO/RTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information must be supplied to state regulatory entities and to EPA when demonstrating compliance with the annual performance standards, and the demonstration will indicate the discrete periods where the alternative standards/emission rates were in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan inclusion and public comment for short-term mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: The short-term reliability mechanism must be explicitly included in a state plan to be utilized by owners/operators of existing affected EGUs, and inclusion must be part of the state's public comment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state plan must specify alternative performance standards for each affected source during events, clearly indicate the emergency alert parameters, the relevant reliability coordinators authorized to issue alerts, and the compliance entities affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism for units with enforceable retirement dates (up to 1 year)
rubrics_metrics.description: States may include an optional reliability assurance mechanism in state plans to enable extensions for units that have committed to cease operation but need to remain online for a discrete, documented reliability need; units could obtain up to a 1-year extension of a cease operation date without a state plan revision if the reliability need is adequately justified and approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extension is limited to the time substantiated through applications and approved by the appropriate EPA Regional Administrator. The date from which an extension can be given is the enforceable date in the state plan, including cease operation dates prior to January 1, 2032.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism — FERC review for >6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: For extension requests greater than 6 months, EPA will seek the advice of FERC and such applications must be submitted to FERC as well as to the appropriate EPA Regional Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for more than 6 months (but ≤12 months) will be reviewed with FERC input; extensions exceeding 12 months must be done through a state plan revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism — Planning Authority certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure reliability claims are sufficiently documented, the unit's relevant reliability Planning Authority(ies) must certify that the claims are accurate and that the identified reliability problem exists and requires the specific relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification by the Planning Authority(ies) is a required element of the application for an extension under this mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability assurance mechanism — scope exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: This mechanism is not intended for units encountering unforeseen delays in installation of control technologies (those issues are addressed through compliance flexibilities) or for units subject to an obligation to operate that is not based on the reliability criteria included here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the compliance flexibilities in section XII.F.2 for installation/permitting delays; use state plan revision/RULOF for other longer-term adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on use and expected utilization
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA does not anticipate heavy utilization of the reliability assurance mechanism if included in state plans; it is intended as an assurance for isolated, unforeseen reliability issues that cannot be addressed through planning or other flexibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA encourages states to consult electric reliability authorities during the state plan process (Meaningful Engagement) to minimize need for these mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent and interagency coordination (MATS Enforcement Response Policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA references prior MATS-era Enforcement Response Policy where narrow, case-by-case administrative orders (up to 1 year) were used when deactivation or delays beyond owner/operator control could have an adverse localized impact on reliability; these orders relied on FERC review to assess reliability claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current mechanism leverages similar concepts: limited extensions, FERC involvement on longer requests, and stringent substantiation requirements; historically these policies were used sparingly.
